text:
Maya: Hi team, on my first day trying to run the repo's Buildkite pipeline. The push step to ECR fails with `no basic auth credentials`. I'm not sure which secret or permission I should request. Repo is under redwood org and I installed it into my account.

ci-bot: Build #7 failed on step "push-image"
```
+ aws ecr get-login-password --region us-west-2
+ docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 222233334444.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
Error response from daemon: login attempt to https://222233334444.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v2/ failed with status: 403 Forbidden
no basic auth credentials
```

jon: welcome! Two quick paths: either the Buildkite agent has an IAM role that can talk to ECR, or the pipeline needs AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY set as secrets. Also confirm ECR_REGISTRY is the right account id.

Maya: I was relying on pipeline env vars from the org but only saw ECR_REGISTRY set. I can't find AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the pipeline settings.

devex-sre: FYI org secrets are only forwarded to builds for repos the GitHub app is installed on. If this repo was added as a fork or private personal copy, GH will not pass org-level secrets.
Also try `aws sts get-caller-identity` in a debug step to see which principal the build is using.

Maya: ran an ad-hoc debug step, got `arn:aws:iam::999988887777:user/maya-onboarding` which is our onboarding IAM user, so envs are present but maybe the user lacks ECR rights.

Ravi: that ARN implies the creds are coming from a pipeline secret tied to your user. Check the IAM policy attached. For ECR pushes the minimum actions we usually grant are: `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken`, `ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability`, `ecr:InitiateLayerUpload`, `ecr:UploadLayerPart`, `ecr:CompleteLayerUpload`, `ecr:PutImage`.

jon: another thing I've seen: the registry host account (222233334444) must match the account for the creds. If you generated creds in a separate AWS account you'll get 403. Run `aws ecr describe-repositories --registry-id 222233334444` to validate access.

devex-sre: I checked the repo in the Buildkite GH app and it was not added (this is a common onboarding gap). I added the repo to the org install and copied a short-lived pipeline secret `ONBOARD_ECR_CREDS` which maps to a temporary IAM user we use for new folks. I also toggled the pipeline to expose `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` for the rebuild.

ci-bot: Rebuild started (by Maya)

ci-bot: Build #8 step "push-image" passed

Maya: Woohoo! Build passed and artifact pushed. Learned that GH app install + matching AWS account + proper ECR permissions are all required. I'll add a checklist to onboarding.

jon: if you want to paste the IAM policy I can suggest a minimal snippet to include in the doc.

Maya: yes please.

Ravi: suggested snippet (onboarding-only, scope down in prod):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "ecr:GetAuthorizationToken",
        "ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability",
        "ecr:InitiateLayerUpload",
        "ecr:UploadLayerPart",
        "ecr:CompleteLayerUpload",
        "ecr:PutImage"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Maya: will add that to onboarding.md along with steps: (1) ensure repo added to Buildkite GH app, (2) verify ECR_REGISTRY matches creds, (3) set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY or use agent IAM role, (4) run `aws sts get-caller-identity` if unsure. Thanks everyone :heart:
